skill.name: date-calculator
skill.description: Use when a question needs exact Gregorian date arithmetic - days between dates, age or duration, working or business days, a deadline N days, weeks or months from a date, the weekday or ISO week of a date, whether a date is a working day, or public or bank holidays for a country or region. Applies to the Date Calculator MCP tools count_days, shift_date, get_holidays and list_locations.
skill.summary: Guides Date Calculator MCP calls for Gregorian date arithmetic, working days, deadlines, and regional holidays.
skill.author: onlinealarmkur

content.user_title: Calculate Dates, Working Days, and Holidays
content.value_statement: Date calculations become unreliable when endpoint rules, weekends, and regional holidays are unclear. This skill guides Date Calculator MCP calls and explains the rules behind each result.
actual_capabilities: Guides count_days calls for date intervals, inclusive periods, ages, and durations.
Configures weekend and holiday exclusions for working-day counts and single-date checks.
Guides shift_date calls for working-day offsets and calendar offsets adjusted to eligible days.
Retrieves weekdays and ISO week information through count_days results.
Uses get_holidays and list_locations for holiday names, dates, and supported country or region codes.
Formats answers with calculation assumptions, tool warnings, and available share links.
limitations: Requires a connected Date Calculator MCP server; the skill contains instructions, not a standalone calculation engine.
Does not support times of day, time zones, non-Gregorian calendars, alarms, reminders, or calendar event creation.
Holiday availability depends on supported locations and service budgets; requests cover at most 11 years and data omits half-day holidays.
Future holidays can change; legal, tax, contract, and payment deadlines require confirmation with the relevant authority.

use_cases.title: Plan delivery dates
use_cases.description: Calculate working-day delivery targets using explicit weekend rules and supported regional holidays.

use_cases.title: Count working days in a reporting period
use_cases.description: Count working days between inclusive period boundaries while stating the country, region, and excluded weekdays.

use_cases.title: Compare public holiday schedules
use_cases.description: Retrieve holiday names and dates for supported destinations when planning travel.

prompt_templates.title: Count a simple interval
prompt_templates.prompt: Count the calendar days from 2027-03-01 to 2027-03-08. Exclude the end date and state the counting rule.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: a date interval with explicit boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Count weekdays inclusively
prompt_templates.prompt: Count working days from 2027-03-01 through 2027-03-31 inclusive. Exclude Saturdays and Sundays, but do not exclude public holidays.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: an inclusive period with weekday exclusions.

prompt_templates.title: Calculate a regional deadline
prompt_templates.prompt: Find 10 working days after 2027-04-01 in Bavaria, Germany. Resolve the region code and exclude Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays. Report warnings.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: region discovery and holiday-aware date shifting.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two date-shifting rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare one working month after 2027-01-15 with one calendar month later rolled to the next weekday. Exclude Saturdays and Sundays, not holidays. Explain both rules.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: distinguish working-unit arithmetic from calendar arithmetic with a final adjustment.

output_examples.input: How many days are between 2027-03-01 and 2027-03-08, excluding the end date?
output_examples.output: 7 calendar days. The start date is counted, and the end date is excluded. No weekdays or holidays are excluded.

output_examples.input: What is five working days after 2027-03-01, excluding Saturdays and Sundays but not holidays?
output_examples.output: Monday, 2027-03-08. The start date is not counted. Saturdays and Sundays are excluded; public holidays are not excluded.

output_examples.input: Can you convert a meeting time from London to Tokyo?
output_examples.output: This service does not support times of day or time zone conversions.

best_practices: Use YYYY-MM-DD dates and resolve ambiguous inputs before requesting calculations.
Specify endpoint inclusion, weekend rules, and holiday exclusions; retrieve region codes instead of guessing.
State the reference date for relative questions and include tool warnings and available calculation links.
anti_patterns: Assuming that selecting a country automatically excludes its public holidays.
Treating excluded-unit month shifts as calendar month shifts without considering roll behavior.
Inventing holiday dates when data is unavailable or presenting calculated deadlines as authoritative legal advice.

faq.question: Does the skill work without an MCP connection?
faq.answer: No. Connect the Date Calculator MCP server before requesting calculations. The skill directs users to its setup documentation.

faq.question: Are both dates counted by default?
faq.answer: No. count_days includes the start date and excludes the end date. Set includeEnd to true for an inclusive interval.

faq.question: Are weekends and public holidays excluded automatically?
faq.answer: No. Set excluded weekdays explicitly. To exclude holidays, enable excludeHolidays and provide a country; regional calendars also require a region.

faq.question: How are months handled when shifting dates?
faq.answer: With exclusions and no roll, shift_date treats all units as working days. Use roll for calendar offsets followed by a working-day adjustment.

faq.question: What happens when holiday data is unavailable?
faq.answer: The skill reports the limitation. It can return a calculation without holiday exclusions only when that difference is clearly stated.

faq.question: Can I rely on the result for an official deadline?
faq.answer: Confirm legal, tax, contract, and payment deadlines with the relevant authority. Future holidays can change, and half-day holidays are not marked.
